questionText: A non-pipelined instruction execution unit operating at $2\text{ GHz}$ takes an average of $6$ cycles to execute an instruction of a program $P$. The unit is then redesigned to operate on a $5$-stage pipeline at $2\text{ GHz}$. Assume that the ideal throughput of the pipelined unit is $1$ instruction per cycle. In the execution of program $P$, $20\%$ instructions incur an average of $2$ cycles stall due to data hazards and $20\%$ instructions incur an average of $3$ cycles stall due to control hazards. The speedup (rounded off to one decimal place) obtained by the pipelined design over the non-pipelined design is _________
explanation:
Step 1: Calculate the average CPI for non-pipelined execution.
$\text{CPI}_{\text{non-pipelined}} = 6$

Step 2: Calculate the average CPI for pipelined execution.
Ideal CPI = $1$
Stalls due to data hazards = $20\% \times 2 = 0.20 \times 2 = 0.40$ cycles
Stalls due to control hazards = $20\% \times 3 = 0.20 \times 3 = 0.60$ cycles

$$\text{CPI}_{\text{pipelined}} = \text{Ideal CPI} + \text{Stalls}_{\text{data}} + \text{Stalls}_{\text{control}} = 1 + 0.40 + 0.60 = 2.0$$

Step 3: Calculate the Speedup.
Since the clock frequency ($2\text{ GHz}$) is identical in both cases, the clock cycle time $T_{\text{clk}}$ remains constant.

$$\text{Speedup} = \frac{\text{CPI}_{\text{non-pipelined}}}{\text{CPI}_{\text{pipelined}}} = \frac{6}{2.0} = 3.0$$

Thus, the speedup obtained is 3.0.
